title: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, DOM, events, JSON, HTTP, REST, and Git vocabulary
objectives: Map HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to an LWC bundle: template, styles, and class.
Explain DOM and events as the live document and the signals that update it.
Read JSON as the usual REST body and HTTP as the request/response protocol.
Use Git vocabulary (working tree, commit, branch) as source history, not the org.
diagnostic_question: An LWC shows a button that calls Apex, receives JSON-looking data, and you must commit the component. Which file is HTML versus CSS versus JavaScript, what is the DOM, what is an HTTP request versus REST, and what Git command records the snapshot?
definition: HTML marks up structure, CSS styles it, and JavaScript behaves. The DOM is the live document tree; events are signals such as click. JSON is a text data format. HTTP is the client-server protocol of requests and responses; REST uses HTTP to act on resources. Git records snapshots of source. LWC HTML templates use a template root and should let LWC update the DOM. ([HTML Templates](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-html.html); [HTTP Overview (MDN)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Overview); [REST API Developer Guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/intro_rest.htm))
why_it_matters: Salesforce UI interviews mix these words. Candidates fail by calling Apex a DOM, calling a change set Git, stuffing business rules in CSS, or concatenating HTML from untrusted JSON. LWC, REST integrations, and Salesforce DX all assume this vocabulary.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a theater production. HTML is the script's scene list—what exists on stage. CSS is costume and lighting. JavaScript is the stage manager calling cues. The DOM is the live stage after the curtain is up. Events are cues: a click is 'enter stage left.' JSON is the call sheet passed to the box office. HTTP is the runner taking a sealed envelope to the office and bringing a reply. REST is the office's resource window: GET the seating chart, POST a reservation. Git is the prompt-book archive of every rehearsal snapshot—not the live audience.
deeper_explanation: LWC HTML templates use a template root. Let LWC manipulate the DOM instead of writing ad-hoc JS DOM surgery. You can bind data, render conditionally, and render lists. CSS in the bundle styles the component; JavaScript is the class. ([HTML Templates](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/lwc/guide/create-components-html.html))

MDN: HTML is the structure of web documents; CSS is presentation; JavaScript is behavior. The DOM is the document represented as objects; events deliver notifications such as user clicks. JSON is a text format for structured data, commonly used in HTTP APIs. ([MDN HTML](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML); [MDN JSON](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Scripting/JSON))

HTTP is a client-server protocol: the user-agent sends requests, the server sends responses. It fetches resources such as HTML and can POST content. REST on Salesforce uses HTTP methods against resource URLs, typically with JSON. ([HTTP Overview](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Overview); [What Is REST? / REST API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.api_rest.meta/api_rest/intro_rest.htm))

Git stores commits—snapshots of files—on branches. Salesforce DX projects are meant to live in Git; the org is not Git. Working tree versus staging versus commit is DEVOPS-003; this lesson is vocabulary only. Do not invent CLI flags.

mental_model.analogy: Theater production: script scenes (HTML), costumes/lights (CSS), stage manager (JavaScript), live stage (DOM), cues (events), call sheet (JSON), runner's envelope (HTTP), box-office resource window (REST), prompt-book archive (Git).
useful_mapping: HTML → what exists in the scene
event → a cue such as click
REST → resource URLs plus HTTP methods
org records → tonight's audience, not the prompt book
where_it_breaks: LWC uses a virtual DOM; you should not treat document.querySelector as the LWC way.
Apex JSON.serialize is server-side, not the browser JSON object.
Git is not a deployment tool by itself (change sets, CLI deploy are later).
REST is not the only Salesforce API (SOAP, Bulk, GraphQL exist).

teach_back_prompt: Using the theater, map HTML, CSS, JavaScript, DOM, events, JSON, HTTP, REST, and Git. Then say why LWC should own the DOM and why Git is not the org.

review_schedule.prompt: Which LWC file is HTML vs CSS vs JS? What does DOM stand for in practice?
HTTP request versus REST resource. JSON versus JavaScript object.
Git commit versus deploying to an org.
Why not innerHTML untrusted JSON into an LWC?
Two-minute interview covering all title terms.

claims.claim: LWC HTML templates use a template root. It is a best practice to let LWC manipulate the DOM instead of writing JavaScript to do it. Templates can bind data, render conditionally, and render lists.
claims.validation: HTML Templates in the LWC Developer Guide.

claims.claim: HTTP is a client-server protocol: clients send requests and servers send responses to fetch resources. HTML is the markup for document structure.
claims.validation: MDN HTTP Overview and MDN HTML landing.

claims.claim: JSON is a text-based data format commonly used when exchanging data with HTTP APIs. Salesforce REST API uses HTTP to access org resources, typically with JSON.
claims.validation: MDN JSON plus REST API introduction.

claims.claim: Salesforce DX is source-driven and intended to work with version control. Git stores source snapshots; it is not the running org and not by itself a deploy mechanism.
claims.validation: Salesforce DX introduction pairing DX with version control.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: HTML structure, CSS look, JavaScript behavior. DOM is the live tree; events are cues. JSON is text data. HTTP is request/response; REST uses it on resources. Git snapshots source, not the org.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: In LWC I put markup in the HTML template, styles in CSS, logic in JS. I let LWC update the DOM. A click is an event that may call Apex or HTTP. REST is HTTP plus resource URLs, usually JSON. I commit in Git before deploy; a commit is not a production change. I do not innerHTML untrusted JSON.

terminology.plain: The scene list: what elements exist.
terminology.precise: HyperText Markup Language for document structure. In LWC, the template file with a template root.
terminology.non_example: Apex class markup is not HTML.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: XML in SOAP: different markup family.
terminology.boundary: LWC directives are HTML-plus, not vanilla HTML only.

terminology.plain: Costumes and lighting: how it looks.
terminology.precise: Cascading Style Sheets for presentation. LWC CSS is scoped to the component bundle.
terminology.non_example: A validation rule is not CSS.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: SLDS: Salesforce's CSS design system, later LWC-009.
terminology.boundary: Do not hide required fields with CSS as a security control.

terminology.plain: The stage manager: behavior in the browser.
terminology.precise: The LWC class file. Not Apex. Runs on the client.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: JSON: data text, not executable JS.
terminology.boundary: LWC JS is not full browser DOM freedom under LWS (later LWC-010).

terminology.plain: The live stage: the document as a tree of objects.
terminology.precise: Document Object Model. LWC prefers template binding over manual DOM writes.
terminology.example: A rendered lightning-button node in the page.
terminology.non_example: The Salesforce data model (objects/fields) is not the DOM.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Virtual DOM: LWC's internal rendering approach mentioned in HTML Templates.
terminology.boundary: shadow DOM / LWS details are later.

terminology.plain: A cue: click, load, custom component event.
terminology.precise: A notification that something happened. LWC uses DOM events and custom events (LWC-005).
terminology.non_example: A Platform Event is a Salesforce messaging feature, not a browser click.
terminology.boundary: This lesson is browser/LWC event vocabulary.

terminology.plain: The call sheet: structured text for data.
terminology.precise: JavaScript Object Notation, a text format. Property names in double quotes; not a JS program.
terminology.non_example: An Apex Map in memory before serialize.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: JavaScript object literal: similar, not identical (JSON cannot hold functions).
terminology.boundary: Apex JSON class is server-side serialization.

terminology.plain: The runner's envelope: request out, response back.
terminology.precise: Application-layer client-server protocol. Methods such as GET and POST, status codes on responses.
terminology.non_example: SOQL inside Apex without an HTTP callout.

terminology.plain: The box-office window: resources addressed over HTTP.
terminology.precise: Representational State Transfer style: HTTP methods on resource URLs. Salesforce REST API is the platform's HTTP+JSON API surface.
terminology.example: PATCH a record URL with a JSON body.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Apex REST @RestResource: your class, still HTTP.
terminology.boundary: Bulk, GraphQL, UI API are other APIs (INT-002).

terminology.plain: The prompt-book archive of source snapshots.
terminology.precise: Distributed version control. Commits on branches. DX projects are designed to live here. Not the org, not a deploy by itself.
terminology.non_example: A change set, or Setup Audit Trail.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: GitHub: a hosting product, not the Git data model.

mechanics.after: Bind properties; handle events in JS

mechanics.after: LWC→Apex or REST resource with JSON body

when_to_use: When naming HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files in an LWC before writing Apex-heavy UI.
When a click (event) must update the DOM through the template rather than innerHTML.
When reading a REST call: HTTP method, JSON body, status—not 'the JSON protocol'.
When a teammate calls a Git commit a production deploy or calls the org a Git repository.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this HTML-CSS-JavaScript lesson as the full LWC events and LMS course (LWC-005).
Do not treat REST vocabulary as the entire API catalog (SOAP, Bulk, GraphQL are INT-002).
Do not teach Git branching strategy here; that is DEVOPS-003.
Do not inject untrusted JSON into HTML and call it templating.
configuration_or_code_location: git status / git log in the project, not in Setup.
Workaround REST: /services/data/ in a sandbox with a session—lab only, never production secrets.

worked_example.scenario: Sandbox LWC labStatusBadge shows a status string from a JS property, styles it with CSS, handles a refresh click, and will later be committed. No production org.
inputs: Click to set Closed in the client for the lab

decisions.because: Structure, presentation, behavior split; LWC template owns the DOM.

decisions.decision: Describe a future Apex call as HTTP under the hood, JSON payload, not as 'sending the DOM'.
git add the four bundle files and commit locally; do not treat commit as deploy.
decisions.because: Git snapshots source; DX still needs a deploy step.
decisions.rejected: Only saving in the org with no Git

configuration_or_code: Comment: REST would be HTTP PATCH with JSON {"Status__c":"Closed"} from Apex, not from CSS.
worked_example.output: Click updates the bound property; template re-renders; CSS still applies; Git can record the files.
verification: No innerHTML in the JS file.
Network panel would show no REST until Apex/HTTP is added—status change is client state (PROG-005).
git status lists the bundle files.
worked_example.self_explanation: HTML showed it, CSS dressed it, JS handled the event, Git would archive it. REST was named, not required for the click lab.

hands_on_lab.environment: VS Code or Web Studio plus a scratch/sandbox; synthetic LWC name labStatusBadge.
starting_state_checks: Git available locally or you simulate add/commit commands on paper if Git is blocked—still write the files.
steps: Create labStatusBadge with HTML template, CSS class, and JS property plus click handler as in the worked example.
Deploy or preview in a sandbox; click and confirm the text changes without innerHTML.
Write a one-line comment mapping a hypothetical REST PATCH plus JSON body.
Run git status (or equivalent) and note which files would be committed; do not push.
guided_completion: If the click does nothing, the event is not wired to the handler name.
If you used innerHTML, rewrite with {labStatus} binding.

evidence: Screenshot or note of git status listing the LWC files.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete the lab LWC from the sandbox.
Do not push secrets. Do not deploy to production.

decision_table.signal: Need color, spacing, or visibility that is not a business rule.

decision_table.not: Apex or a validation rule pretending to be styling.

decision_table.signal: Need a history of source files.
decision_table.not: Treating Setup or the org as version control, or commit as deploy.

querySelector as the first LWC habit.

You are looking at HTTP, not Git.

interview_questions.question: Explain HTML, CSS, JavaScript, DOM, events, JSON, HTTP, REST, and Git in a Salesforce UI context.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: HTML structure, CSS look, JS behavior. DOM is the live tree; events are clicks. JSON is data text. HTTP is request/response; REST uses it on resources. Git snapshots source, not the org.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I map those onto an LWC bundle and a Network panel. I let the template own the DOM. I call Apex or REST from JS, not from CSS. I do not confuse Platform Events with click events. I commit in Git then deploy separately. I never innerHTML untrusted JSON.
interview_questions.example: labStatusBadge bundle plus a comment about HTTP PATCH JSON.
tradeoffs: LDS/Apex vs raw REST from the client

interview_questions.question: Why does LWC tell you not to manipulate the DOM yourself first?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The HTML Templates guide says let LWC manipulate the DOM. Bindings and lists stay consistent and safer than innerHTML.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Ad-hoc querySelector fights the engine and opens XSS if you inject JSON as HTML. I bind properties and handle events. Advanced shadow/LWS rules come later. Interviewers want that default.
interview_questions.example: Bind {labStatus} in the LWC template instead of assigning innerHTML = payload from an API string.

interview_questions.question: Walk a button that will PATCH an Account via an API.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: HTML button, CSS optional, JS event, HTTP PATCH, JSON body, REST resource URL, Apex or named credential later. Git commits the LWC.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The click is an event. JS should not hold the session secret. Prefer Apex callout or LDS over raw browser REST with a session. HTTP is the protocol; JSON is the body; REST is the resource style. I still name Git as where the LWC source lives. I do not PATCH from CSS.
interview_questions.example: onclick={handleSave} → Apex → HTTP callout with JSON.
tradeoffs: UI API vs REST sObject vs Apex
weak_answer_warnings: Storing session Id in the JS file in Git

interview_questions.question: Admin says the org is our Git. How do you answer?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: The org is the running system. Git is source snapshots. DX expects version control; deploy is separate.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I explain working tree and commit as vocabulary, not a branching lecture. Change sets are not Git. Two developers need Git to merge HTML/CSS/JS. I invite them to DEVOPS-001/003 for metadata versus data. I do not mock Setup; I split concerns.
interview_questions.example: git commit of lwc/labStatusBadge versus change set upload.

interview_questions.question: Styles not applying. Is it HTML, CSS, JS, or DOM?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check the CSS file and class names in HTML first, then whether JS rendered the node at all.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: If the markup is missing, it is HTML/template. If the node exists in the DOM inspector without rules, CSS selector or LWC scoping. If a class is toggled in JS, the event path is wrong. I do not start with REST. Git blame can show who last changed the CSS.
interview_questions.example: class="labBadge" in HTML but .labBage typo in CSS.
tradeoffs: SLDS utility classes vs custom CSS

interview_questions.question: API tester shows XML. You expected JSON. Vocabulary check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You may be on SOAP, or REST with an Accept/Content-Type that is not JSON.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: REST typically JSON on Salesforce, SOAP is XML. HTTP headers negotiate format. I look at the URL path /services/data versus /services/Soap. I do not call XML 'the DOM' even though HTML has a DOM. Git is irrelevant unless the wrong spec was committed.
interview_questions.example: Workaround REST /sobjects/Account/ versus SOAP partner WSDL.
tradeoffs: REST vs SOAP for the same Account
weak_answer_warnings: JSON is the only Salesforce API

interview_questions.question: When would you skip custom JS and stay in HTML template plus base components?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When lightning-record-form or template conditionals already express the UI without a custom event storm.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: PROG-005 already said prefer base components before Apex. Same for JS: if HTML conditional rendering plus a base form works, I do not invent a DOM framework. I add JS for events and client state. I add HTTP/REST when the browser must talk to a resource. I still commit whatever I add in Git.
interview_questions.example: lightning-record-form instead of a custom HTML form plus REST PATCH from JS.
follow_ups: When must you use custom events?

interview_questions.question: Teach the nine title terms with the theater and where it breaks.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Script is HTML, costumes CSS, stage manager JS, live stage DOM, cues events, call sheet JSON, runner HTTP, box office REST, prompt book Git. It breaks on virtual DOM and Git not deploying.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk a rehearsal: markup, look, cue, live tree, click, JSON call sheet, HTTP envelope, REST window, archive the prompt book. I then say LWC does not want ad-lib DOM, Apex serialize is backstage, REST is not the only window, and Git does not move the audience (org). I show the three LWC files.
